 Marc Marquez, Di Giannantonio in tense exchange over Bezzecchi clash
 MotoGP’s cameras caught a tense exchange between Marquez and Di Giannantonio
 Lewis Duncan 08 Nov 2026 Share Fabio Di Giannantonio (left), Marc Marquez (centre) © Gold and Goose Prefer Crash.Net on Google See our stories more often Add A behind-the-scenes MotoGP video has revealed a tense exchange between Marc Marquez and Fabio Di Giannantonio over the former’s clash with Marco Bezzecchi in the Qatar sprint.
 Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi needs to stop Marquez from outscoring him by eight points across the Qatar Grand Prix weekend to keep his fading title hopes alive to Portugal.
 But that took a serious knock on Saturday in the sprint when the pair collided in the sprint on lap four at Turn 1 in a hugely controversial incident.
 Bezzecchi crashed as a result of the contact, while Marquez went on to win the race to set up his first title match point for today’s race.
 Show Instagram Embedded Content Loading this video will expose you to potential cookies and tracking by the provider “You have to look before closing the line” 
 Marquez said he didn’t do anything strange in that moment, as the FIM MotoGP stewards also cleared him of any wrongdoing.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Bezzecchi offered a reserved review of the incident when speaking to TNT .
 “You saw already the images,” he said.
 “At the end, I tried to keep my line, and the contact happened, so at the end I couldn't really do anything to avoid it.
 “At the end, the one that crashed was me, but it’s like this. So we move forward, and we try to bounce back tomorrow.”
 However, VR46 Ducati rider Fabio Di Giannantonio seems to fully back Bezzecchi in this incident, following a tense exchange with Marquez.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT A video posted by the official MotoGP website captured Di Giannantonio telling Marquez: “Man, you have to look before closing the line like that. He was on the inside.”
 Marquez responded: “I didn’t do anything unusual. I took that line every lap.”
 Di Giannantonio then added: “He went up the inside; it was a hard impact.”

 “No, he was the one who,” Martin says, before being cut off.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Ducati team orders will be harder to enforce 
 Di Giannantonio and Marquez already have a tense relationship, following a collision between the pair at the US Grand Prix earlier this season.
 The Italian also races for Marquez’s arch rival Valentino Rossi’s team, and has been entrenched in the VR46 Academy during his time with the Ducati satellite squad.
 But Di Giannantonio’s comments also suggest he has little desire to aid Marquez’s title bid should Ducati decide to employ team orders.
